- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to align with mean-reversion toward recent 10-day average.
- Model frequently overreacts to sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns negative after a positive streak, reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; apply a 1–3% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model underperforms; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for low sentiment bias.
- When sentiment is high but price is trending down, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 3–5 days to reflect sentiment divergence.
